The first four seconds

Meet the machine

Sumhow is a calculator with most of its keys missing. The screen names a number. The keypad gives you three or four keys and nothing else. Reach the number in the fewest presses.

Step one

Every unit tells you what it is before you open it

The target, the par, and the exact keys you will have. That is the whole briefing. Below it, the chapter's units sit in a grid with the stars you have earned on each, so you always know where you left off.

Roots, unit 9 of 96
Step two

The keys that are gone are really gone

Missing keys are empty sockets in the chassis, not greyed-out buttons. You are holding a broken object and making it work anyway. The machine resolves left to right with no order of operations: on this calculator, 3 + 4 × 2 is 14. That one fact is where most of the difficulty lives.

  • Undo and Clear are free. Experiment as much as you like.
  • Divide refuses anything that is not a whole number. It will, however, accept zero.
  • Nine digits on the screen. Push past them and the machine has something to say about it.
Step three

Par is the truth

Every unit has a par: the fewest presses it can possibly be done in, worked out by the game itself, not guessed by a designer. Match it and you get three stars and a card that says so. Beat your own score later if you want. Nothing is ever locked behind failing.

  • 15chapters
  • 1,020units
  • 0timers or lives

You already know how to work a calculator.That is the entire tutorial. The first unit clicks in about four seconds.

Then it starts changing the rules

One new rule a chapter

The first four chapters teach the instrument. Every chapter after that changes exactly one thing about how the machine behaves, and the puzzles are built around it.

Echo: equals repeats the last operation

Press 4, times, equals, equals, equals and watch the number run. In Echo, the equals key is a tool, and the shortest route to a target is rarely the obvious one.

Chapter 2

Decay: a key that dies

Two multiplications left in this unit. Ever. Spend them early and you are stuck adding your way home. Each chapter has one idea like this: a key that fires twice, a memory key that banks the screen, results that wrap at a thousand, a screen that stays dark until you press equals.

  • Warm Up, Seven Sisters, The Sticky Key, Mirror teach the machine
  • Roots, Echo, Decay, Stutter, Memory, Wraparound, The Toll, Below Zero, Blind each bend one rule
  • And one more chapter that opens only when the machine decides you have earned it

Units on the bench

Every chapter, its keys, and how far you have gotten, on one sheet. Jump anywhere you have unlocked. Come back to any unit to chase the third star.

The other way to read a calculator

Word Mode

A question is asked. The answer is a word. You type the number that spells it when the screen is upside down.

"Texas tea. Black gold."

The readout under the digits shows what your number spells right now, live, so you never have to memorize the alphabet before you start. 710 reads OIL. 5508 reads BOSS. 07734 says hELLO, and yes, the leading zero counts.

  • Ninety-six trivia words, from three letters to nine
  • Some words need a digit the keypad does not have. Build it with arithmetic first.
  • Revealing a word is always free

If you do the Wordle before coffee, this is the next one.One unit a morning, or a whole chapter on a rainy Sunday.

Make it yours

Dress the machine

Forty-three skins in seven packs. Vaporwave, Leopard, Terrazzo, Blueprint, Starfield, Picnic. Every one reskins the whole chassis, keys and all, and you can try any of them on first.

Same machine, different mood

Skins change the chassis, the keys, the screen glow, and the menu behind them. The puzzle underneath never changes, so pick whatever makes you want to pick the phone up.

43 skins7 packsTry before you choose

The menu dresses up too

Pick a skin and the whole app follows: the unit cards, the chapter rail, the bench. Two menus, same chapter, nothing in common but the numbers.

Or go full Leopard

Same Warm Up chapter, same unit 4, same 1089 to make. Completely different afternoon.

The drawer

Some numbers make the machine react

There is a second game underneath this one, and nobody in the app will explain it to you. Certain numbers wake the machine up. Certain mistakes do something other than fail. There is a drawer with nineteen slots, and most of them are empty when you start.

Scratch mode

A full calculator with every key live and no target, so the secrets are findable at all.

Nineteen slots

Found ones show the number and a word. Unfound ones show nothing but that they exist.

We are not saying more

That is the rule, in the app and on this page. Find five and something opens.

Somehow, you'll get there.

Every screenshot on this page is Sumhow running on iPhone. Download it, make 6 with a 3, and see if you can stop.
